text:
lina: heads-up: ran the projectize migration on staging and hit a batch of failing jobs. Looks like old service API keys that relied on implicit org-scope are blocked after the RBAC tightening.

carlos: can you paste an example error?

lina: sure. job log: `403 Forbidden: token lacks required scope (project:write)` even though the service key used to work. Request was:
```
POST /v1/ingest
Authorization: ApiKey sk_live_OLD_123
X-Project: proj-7
```
The token validation returns claim `scope: org:full` for some keys and `scope: project:proj-7:write` for others.

jing: sounds like we've been issuing a mix of token types historically. The migration rule expects explicit project claims unless key metadata maps to an org-admin role.

lina: right. Two classes of problematic keys: 1) legacy long-lived keys created pre-projectize with implicit org-level entitlement, and 2) machine-user keys created via onboarding that never got mapped to a project.

carlos: proposal: introduce a compatibility layer in the token-authority that does runtime token-exchange for legacy keys: when validation sees `scope: org:*` but the request includes X-Project, attempt to mint short-lived project-scoped token if mapping exists. If mapping missing, return 403 with explicit remediation.

jing: I worry about silent escalation. That exchange must only be allowed for trusted internal principals (not external integrations or contractor keys). Also audit every exchange and surface in console.

lina: agreed. my migration checklist idea:
- enumerate all keys with `scope: org:*` and owners
- create mapping table entries for keys owned by internal services to project ids
- enable exchange-for-known-mappings behind feature flag `migrate.projectize.exchange`
- run canary for a subset of services
- flip to deny for unknown keys and notify owners with remediation steps

carlos: for step 2 we can auto-suggest mappings by correlating recent X-Project headers and last-seen project metadata. But require a human review before auto-apply.

jing: also add conservative default: even with a mapping, minted token must be the least privilege (project:read) until the service owner annotates required perms. Avoid granting write by default.

ops-bot: FYI: enabling `migrate.projectize.exchange` will trigger config change and needs a 1h maintenance window for dedicated clusters per infra policy.

lina: noted. Action items: Lina -> generate inventory of org-scoped keys (today), Carlos -> prototype token-exchange flow and logging schema (3 days), Jing -> add policy: only allow exchange for internal principals and default to read (2 days). Ops -> schedule maintenance window.

carlos: quick sketch of exchange call I have in mind:
```
POST /internal/v1/token-exchange
Authorization: Bearer token-authority-svc
Body: {"subject_key":"sk_live_OLD_123","requested_project":"proj-7","requested_scope":"project:proj-7:read"}
Response: {"access_token":"ephemeral_proj_tok","expires_in":600, "granted_scope":"project:proj-7:read"}
```
All calls generate audit event `token_exchange` with fields: subject_key_id, requester, requested_project, requested_scope, granted_scope, mapping_id, decision.

jing: make sure audit-bot ingestion can parse `mapping_id` as string and we include `owner_contact` so the alerts page can link to owner.

audit-bot: noted. Add `owner_contact` and `mapping_reviewed_at` to event schema.

lina: for remediation UX: console should list affected keys with buttons: "Add mapping", "Rotate to project-key", "Schedule migration". We'll coordinate with devex.

carlos: long-term: deprecate long-lived org keys for service-to-service traffic. Encourage short-lived project-scoped service tokens via our token-service and adopt k8s-style service accounts with projected tokens.

jing: +1. Also add an enforcement rule: after 90 days, disallow creation of new org-scoped service keys. Put this in the authz roadmap.

lina: ok i'll open a follow-up RFC for the exchange behaviour and add the migration checklist in the PR. will post link here ASAP.

carlos: small security note: ensure token-exchange logs are scrubbed of raw key values before shipping to ELK. Only log key IDs.

jing: and add rate limits to the exchange endpoint to prevent abuse.

lina: thanks all. next step: inventory first, then prototype. I'll DM owners of the top-10 keys.

ops-bot: Reminder: maintenance windows must be requested 48h in advance for dedicated clusters.

carlos: thx. will prioritize prototype so we can validate with a canary group this week. :thumbsup:
